packs.title: Gardens, Art & Port
packs.promise: Find a garden crossing, compare art and follow the city toward its working port.

q.s: Let one displayed work change a small composition of your own.
st: From Shukkeien’s main gate take the 150 m / 2 min public street link to the museum; allow signed entry and ticket finding. Use valid collection admission: standard 510 yen adult or 310 university. High-school and younger and 65+ are free; bring official age or eligibility proof. Listed disability holders and one carer enter the collection free with the required certificate. The current adult garden-and-collection ticket is 660 yen; special exhibitions are separate. Normal collection hours are 09:00–17:00, last entry 16:30; check Monday, 25 December–1 January and display-change closures and their exceptions.
Choose an interpreted work in an open collection room. Note its displayed title or a precise identification, then select one visible shape, interval or colour relationship.
Make a small drawing or three written lines that use that relationship in a different arrangement. Do not copy a whole work or claim to speak for its maker.
Change one part and explain what became clearer. Keep your observation, first version and revision together.

q.s: Collect evidence of material, space and viewpoint in an open collection.
st: Begin the separate Hijiyama outing at Hijiyama-shita around 10:00. The actual uphill route to the western public museum approach is 700 m / 11 min; allow 25–35 min with slope, stairs and rests, then 10–15 min for the signed plaza, door and admission.

Use valid collection admission before 16:30: standard 350 yen adult, university 250, high-school or 65+ 150; junior-high and younger are free. International students need a student card or accepted prefectural priority card for free entry; people with dependent residency need status ID. Listed disability or medical-certificate holders and attendants need accepted certificates for free entry. Special exhibitions are separate. Hours are 10:00–17:00; Mondays or the next weekday after a holiday and 27 December–1 January are closed, with listed exceptions. The collection is free on the third Sunday; 3 November is a published free day.

In open collection rooms choose three displayed works or interpreted features: one with an interesting material, one using surrounding space and one that changes when you change viewpoint. Record each identity and its visible evidence.
Write which decision most changed your attention and why. Follow permitted circulation; no particular work is guaranteed.

q.s: Build a small account of work from interpreted objects.
st: Take the actual 2.2 km / 31 min street walk from Wharf Park to the museum’s southern public approach; allow 40–50 min, then 10–15 min for the signed door and valid admission. Enter before 16:30. Standard adult admission is 100 yen; 65+, high-school and other under-18 admission 50, with official age proof for seniors; middle-school and younger are free. Hours are 09:00–17:00. Avoid Mondays, December and January Tuesdays, the weekday after a public holiday, 29 December–3 January and temporary closures; check the current calendar. Listed child free-day exceptions and 3 November free entry follow the municipal guide.

In the open collection choose three interpreted objects connected with local work or everyday life. Record each displayed name and its stated job; no particular tool or temporary exhibition is required.
For each object, identify a visible feature that might help that job. Mark your explanation as an inference unless the label confirms it.

Compare the three objects in a short table. Leave time for the 350 m / 5 min public return approach to Ujina 2-chome, signed platform finding and a town-bound Route 5 tram. Allow 10–15 min for that street approach, then 35–50 min for the signed platform, wait and ride to Hiroshima Station; the current weekday ride example is 20 min. The return is a separate applicable fare, normally another 240 yen adult.

packs.title: Streets & Memory
packs.promise: Read a shopping street, preserved buildings and the river through two connected walks.

q.s: Collect facts from the school museum without copying personal messages.
st: From Hondori use the 200 m / 3 min public street approach and find the signed museum entrance. Individual visitor admission is free, 09:00–17:00, closed 28 December–4 January. This is the preserved visitor west wing, not permission to enter active school grounds.
Read open interpretation about the building and its changing uses. Collect three clearly stated facts, each with the display or panel that supports it.
For one fact, identify a visible building detail or reproduction that helps explain it. Keep what you read separate from what you infer.
Write your three facts and that link without transcribing personal names, chalk messages or testimony. Continue by public streets to the former bank.

q.s: Write the river from three observed distances on one dry public edge.
st: After the National Hall’s North Exit, follow open public paths and the bridge crossing to the upper east-bank public paving. The actual link is 190 m / 3 min; allow crossings and finding. Use dry daylight conditions, not a low river terrace, boat landing or café.
From a position clear of circulation, choose a near edge, a middle-distance movement and a far shape. Describe only what is actually present; no boat or reflection is required.
Write three short frames or make three small drawings. Reorder them once and explain how the new order changes your sense of movement.
Keep both versions and continue north by the upper public path outside the Dome fence.

q.s: Turn a formal garden view into two different arrangements.
st: From the Dome use the selected 650 m / 9 min public route via Aioi-dori; allow 15–20 min for crossings and finding the southeast upper garden rim. Visit in safe daylight on an open public path; ordinary garden viewing is free.
Look into the sunken formal garden from a permitted path. Choose two repeated edges or shapes actually visible, using beds, paths or planting as found rather than expecting flowers.
Make a small pattern drawing or three written lines, then change one repetition to alter the emphasis. Stay outside the beds.
Keep your first and revised versions and explain the change. Finish the walk from the open upper park paths.
